findings.text: — s26 measures "once the figure review is stored and complete, the same run is landed" in a fresh temporary crew home, but in production a run refused for its missing figure review carries `admission_landing: refused` and `_refusal_holds` (queue_landing.py:268-296) is keyed on `code_stamp` and the code review's `review_stamp` only; storing the figure review moves neither stamp, so the refusal still holds and the run is never re-judged — the exact state the section exists to clear.

— s28's first case drives `advance_waiting_requests` directly and counts `project_section_readiness` through a patch, but the new key applies only when `_READINESS_PASS_ACTIVE` is set (queue_admission.py:2233); nothing in the case enters `readiness_pass()` or `project_read()`, so with the bounded read at its default True `_readiness_rows` takes the `section_readiness_rows` branch and returns before the whole-project call, making the count zero on the base revision and on the fixed revision alike and leaving the stated negative control unable to discriminate.

— s29's three cases are an added-and-reproducing failure, an added-and-flaky failure, and no added failure; no case has the candidate and main failing the same id, which is the ordinary state on a red main and is the state s29's own Why records ("Both now fail on main 9430f8e207").

— s30's first deliverable names four ways an earlier request can be held (a claim, a gate, a backoff, a plan review), while its gate measures only the claim case; a node that narrows `_earlier_overlapping_request` to skip claim-held requests alone passes all three cases and leaves the other three holds fencing later requests.

— s30 bundles two independent repairs: the overlap rule in `_earlier_overlapping_request` and the ranking guarantee of a priority override under `fair_share_admission_order`/`weighted_project_order`; they share no code path, case 3 is the only arm that measures the second, and one write scope (`queue_admission.py`) is asked to carry both.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `select_review_for_head` resolves at reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:113 and is called with no rubric at reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:861; `_readiness_rows` resolves at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2195 with the stated key; `_READINESS_PASS_ACTIVE` is the contextvar at queue_admission.py:2275; `_earlier_overlapping_request` resolves (definition at queue_admission.py:652, call at :4120); `landing_measure.py` exists with `importer_population` and `measure_run`; merges 30fbd6294e, 051c9c0fa3 and 9430f8e207 all resolve as commits, and head 9385b998b belongs to power_convertor so its absence from this repository is not a broken pointer.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s26's second case lands a run whose figure review arrives with no prior refusal stamped, so the refusal-hold path that production takes is never exercised.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the five sections name no node-local or scratchpad evidence path; the gate logs they rely on are the run's own manifest test_logs, and s23 remains the only evidence fragment they cite.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the five new test names each state the mechanism (`test_the_lander_waits_for_every_owed_review`, `test_a_landing_refusal_names_its_remedy`, `test_a_pass_builds_each_project_once`, `test_the_lander_measures_the_population`, `test_a_held_request_holds_nothing_behind_it`), and none carries a plan label, stage word, version tag or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — each root cause matches the code it cites: `select_review_for_head` discards figure-rubric records outright (recovery_review_subject.py:142-154), which is why the lander reads only the code review; the readiness key does carry plan and refs; and `order` is built once per pass from every placeable request, so a request the pass has already held stays in `order[:index]` and is counted as an overlap, exactly as s30 states.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — s30 carries two independent deliverables (hold semantics, and priority ranking across sessions) with one write scope and one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — plan-section-depends-on now declares s27→s26, s29→s26 and s30→s28, every target resolves to a section that exists, and no section among the five consumes output it fails to declare.
